neighbours.label: ' a' right after a limiting 'just' or 'only', where a small share is about to be named ('just a few of', 'only a portion', 'only a tiny fraction'); the output direction promotes ' subset', ' fraction', ' portion'. The − pole takes ' a' before an unrestricted part ('owns a majority', 'and a part of').
fire: Wolves, lynx and beavers are just a few of the animals returning to the valley.
The exhibition displays only a fraction of the museum's collection.
Typing, filing and answering calls are just a handful of the tasks involved.
So far the survey has reached only a small share of households.
The photos here are just a sample of what the archive holds.
Astronomers have catalogued only a tiny part of the galaxy's stars.
Jazz, folk and choral music are just a few of the styles on the programme.
The report quotes only a portion of the original letter.
quiet: Wolves, lynx and beavers are returning to a valley that had lost them.
The exhibition displays a painting from the museum's collection.
Typing, filing and answering calls can fill a whole working day.
So far the survey has reached a majority of households.
The photos here come from a box found in the archive.
Astronomers have catalogued the stars with a new telescope.
Jazz, folk and choral music share a stage on the programme.
The report quotes the original letter in a long footnote.

notes: Probe: 'just a few of' 0.60, 'only a portion' 0.66, 'a random subset' 0.28; 'bought a car' 0.00, 'owns a majority' 0.02. Near misses keep the sentence and an ' a' but drop the limiting just/only.
